01Dashboard SummaryOVERVIEW▶

A working generator for a replacement snow thrower push key, built to Izzy’s specification as the Claude Fable 5.2 entry in an AI-versus-human design challenge. Change any parameter and the key rebuilds in 3D; export it as STL and quad OBJ for slicing. The page also holds the full parameter table, the design decisions, the benchmark log the spec asks for, and print and test notes. Terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

At a glanceSpec-default key: 60.5 × 27 × 17 mm, stem 33.5 mm, about 8.9 cm³. The mesh is closed, about 99% quads, and was re-checked from the exported STL. First closed model 12:13 after the go; 19 spec issues logged with their workarounds.

03The ChallengeBRIEF▶

Izzy wrote one specification for a replacement push key for a snow thrower and handed it to several AI tools and to human engineers, to see who returns the cleanest design. This page is the Claude Fable 5.2 entry, run at medium effort. An identical brief goes to Claude Opus 5.5 in its own thread.

Izzy’s invitation“I have a challenge. I wrote up specs for a push key on a snow thrower. Gemini, ChapGPT, F360 AI are in the challenge. I think you use Claude. All the info is in the file that details EVERYTHING (I hope). I am looking to see which one comes up with the cleanest design. I am including photos if the AI will accept them. And I would like to invite you to be in the challenge. If you are interested. I will send you the specs to review and see how you do against the AI’s and me. May the squirrely-est (is that word?) brain rule!”
Original key, injection molded. Photo supplied by Izzy. Left: grip face. Right: side view.
  • PartA single-piece key: a stem that pushes into a spring-loaded switch barrel, a guard collar that stops it, and a handle sized for heavy winter gloves.
  • MotionPure linear push-in and pull-out. No twisting load, so the stem only has to survive axial force and the latch in its locking window.
  • ParametricEvery dimension driven by a named parameter, so a change never breaks the model.
  • SymmetryStrict bilateral symmetry about the long axis, with the guard as the datum.
  • MaterialPETG, printed flat on the bed, 4 or more perimeters, 35 to 40% gyroid infill.
  • BenchmarkEach entrant logs the time from prompt to finished model, and every spec ambiguity with the workaround used. Both are in Benchmark Log.
  • ExportsSTL and a quad OBJ only for now. A native Fusion model may follow in a separate thread.
  • Stem lengthUse 33.5 mm, the sum 22.0 + 6.0 + 5.5, where the table says 34.0.
  • RecessThe stem recess goes on both faces.
  • One pieceA single part printed flat, as the spec says.
  • ThingiverseA two-piece model of this key exists on Thingiverse [1]. It is listed for documentation only and was not used for this geometry; see Thingiverse Model.
Where to startOpen Key Generator, change any value in the side panel, and watch the key rebuild. Export gives a zip with the STL, the quad OBJ and the parameter table.

Thingiverse Thing 53277. Image supplied by Swami. Left: the whole key. Right: one of the two identical halves, lying flat as printed.
Not usedThe Thingiverse model and this image were not used to generate the 3D model on this page. Swami set that rule before the run. The geometry was built before this image was looked at, from Izzy’s spec and the photo of the original key alone, and it has not been changed since to match it.

  • SourceThis entry takes every dimension from Izzy’s spec. Nothing was measured or traced from the Thingiverse model.

05Key GeneratorGENERATOR▶

This is the working part of the page: a live 3D model of the push key that you can reshape, inspect and export. Every dimension in Izzy’s spec is a control in the side panel. Change a value and the key rebuilds at once, usually in under a tenth of a second, from the same mesh the exports use. Press maximize at the top right of the viewer to give it the whole window.

The key is colour coded by part: StemGuardHandleGrip & lanyard Each group of controls in the side panel carries the colour of the part it changes, and the 3MF export keeps the same colours.

View and display controls run along the top, light and section cut along the bottom, a view cube sits in the corner, and the side panel holds every parameter, measuring and export. The hot keys work once you have clicked in the 3D view.

  • STLBinary, millimetres, triangles only. This is the file for Orca or PrusaSlicer.
  • OBJThe same surface as quads wherever possible (about 99% at the defaults), grouped as handle, guard and stem, with every parameter value written in the header.
  • 3MFOne closed mesh with four named materials, Stem, Guard, Handle, and Grip and lanyard, in the same colours as the viewer, assigned triangle by triangle. Slicers that read standard 3MF colours can map each to a filament; that import has not been tested from here.
  • ParametersA CSV with name, unit, expression, value and comment columns, laid out for the parameter table in Fusion. The import has not been tested from here.
  • SettingsA JSON file with every value, the derived values and the mesh facts.
  • On the bedBy default the export is lifted so its lowest point sits at Z = 0. Untick the box to keep it centred on the mid-plane.
Everything stays hereThe model is computed in this browser tab. Nothing is uploaded, and nothing is saved until you export a file.

07Design DecisionsDESIGN▶

How each part of the spec became geometry. Where the spec left a shape open, the choice is exposed as a parameter and recorded in Benchmark Log.

FeaturePartHow it is modelledDriven by
Stem bodyStemA bar 9.5 wide and 4.1 thick, 33.5 long from the guard facestem_width, stem_thickness, stem_length
Edge rim and recessed webStemA 1.4 mm full-thickness rim around a web 6.7 wide and 1.3 thick, recessed equally on both faces, from 1.4 mm off the guard to one rim width before the windowstem_edge_rim, stem_recess_start
Locking windowStemA square 6.0 mm through-hole starting 22.0 mm from the guard face, with 1.75 mm walls beside itstem_cutout_start, stem_cutout_size
Diamond tipStemThe last 5.5 mm thins from 4.1 to a 2.6 mm nose, a diamond when seen from the side. Two other readings are one click awaystem_tip_distance, stem_tip_nose, stem_tip_style
Side notchStemOn both edges: a 3-point arc 4.0 wide and 1.0 deep starting at 14.0, then a straight taper that leaves the arc tangentially and meets the edge at 22.0, exactly where the window startsstem_notch_start, stem_notch_depth, stem_notch_span, stem_notch_taper
Leading chamfersStem0.5 mm at 45° on the tip corners in plan and on the nose in thicknessstem_chamfer
CollarGuardA 3.0 × 18.0 × 11.0 block; its stem-side face is the datum, X = 0guard_length, guard_width, guard_height
Collar corners and edgesGuardA 2.0 mm radius on the four corners of the outline and a 0.5 mm bevel around both facesguard_corner_radius, guard_edge_break
Handle outlineHandle27.0 wide for the first 5.0 mm with 5.0 mm rounded back corners, then a single arc of radius 27.82 mm, tangent to the full width, down to 12.0 at the guardhandle_width, handle_neck_width, handle_transition, handle_corner_radius, handle_outline_style
Handle thicknessHandle17.0 thick over the same 5.0 mm zone, then the same kind of arc down to 9.5 at the guard, giving the bulb seen in the side photohandle_height, handle_neck_height, handle_thickness_style
Edge roundingHandleA 4.0 mm radius where both grip faces meet the outline, measured as true distance from the edge so it wraps the back corners evenlyhandle_edge_radius
Grip groovesGripFlat-bottomed grooves 1.2 wide and 0.6 deep across both grip faces, 2.2 apart, kept 1.2 clear of the hole; as many as fit, up to 3 on each side of the hole (5 at the defaults)rib_count, rib_pitch, rib_width, rib_depth, rib_hole_clearance
Lanyard holeGripA 4.5 mm hole straight through the thickness at the middle of the handle lengthlanyard_hole_dia, lanyard_hole_offset
  • ParametricOne list of named parameters drives everything. No dimension is typed twice; stem_length, the web sizes and the arc radius are computed from the others.
  • ConstrainedThere are no sketches to drift. Each feature is positioned from the datum by formula, so a change cannot leave a feature behind.
  • MirrorOnly one half of the outline is built; the other half is its mirror image across the long axis, and the bottom is the mirror of the top. Symmetry is exact by construction.
  • DatumThe guard face the stem starts from is X = 0. Stem distances are measured forward from it, the guard and handle backward.
  • Push actionThe window walls, the tip beyond the window and the rim stay at full thickness, so the latch bears on solid plastic in both directions.
  • GlovesThe handle keeps the spec’s enlarged 27 × 17 mm section, rounded edges, and grooves on both faces.
How the solid is builtThe key is laid out from above as a grid of four-sided cells that follow its outline: stations along the length, lanes across the width. Each cell corner gets a height, the bottom mirrors the top, and a wall is added wherever two neighbouring cells differ in height or a cell has no neighbour. That is why almost every face is a quad, why holes and the window have clean walls, and why the mesh closes without any repair step.
  • TipThe diamond tip is read as a wedge in thickness because it helps the stem enter the barrel and keeps the full width for the latch. If Izzy meant a diamond in plan, set stem_tip_style to plan.
  • NotchThe notch is read as a teardrop: arc first, then a ramp. The ramp ending exactly at the window start suggests the latch rides it into the window.
  • Handle arcA convex arc gives the fullest grip for gloves. The s-curve option is closer to the original key in the photo.
  • Root cornerThe spec gives no fillet where the stem meets the guard. None was added, because the guard face is the stop. It is the first place to look if a printed stem snaps.

  • ModelClaude Fable 5.2 at medium effort, working alone in one thread.
  • InputsThe spec file and the composite photo of the original key. The Thingiverse model and its photo were not used.
  • MethodThe geometry was written as code and checked by counting edges: a closed mesh has every edge shared by exactly two faces. Random parameter sets were then tried to find values that break it.
  • ChecksAt spec values the exported STL was read back independently: 0 open edges, and a surface with exactly two through-holes, the locking window and the lanyard hole. 1,200 random parameter sets all stayed closed, apart from sets where the guard was made smaller than the stem or handle, which the viewer flags.
  • Not doneNo test print, no fit check in a real switch, and no native Fusion or STEP file.
09Print and TestPRINT▶

Nothing here has been printed yet. These are the spec’s print settings, the one orientation problem the spec leaves open, and a checklist for the physical test Izzy describes.

  • MaterialPETG.
  • Perimeters4 or more. At a 0.4 mm nozzle that makes the 1.4 mm rim and the window walls solid.
  • Infill35 to 40% gyroid. Only the handle and guard are thick enough to hold any.
  • OrientationFlat on the bed, grip face down, so the layers run along the stem and the push and pull loads do not try to split them.
Supports are neededThe key is symmetric about its mid-plane, so lying flat it touches the bed only under the handle. The guard overhangs by 3.0 mm and the stem floats 6.45 mm up for its whole length. Turn on supports under the guard and stem (tree or organic supports peel off the stem most cleanly), or print the key standing on one long edge, which trades supports for a narrower footprint and a seam along the grip.
CheckTopicHowPass when
Stem widthFitCalipers across the stem9.5 mm, and it slides into the switch barrel without forcing
Stem thicknessFitCalipers on the rim, not the web4.1 mm
StopFunctionPush the key fully inThe guard face seats and the switch closes
LatchFunctionPush in, let go, then pullThe spring latch drops into the window and the key stays until pulled
Pull-outStrengthTwenty insert and pull cycles with gloves onNo whitening or cracking at the window walls or at the stem root
RootStrengthLight sideways load on the handle while insertedNo crack where the stem meets the guard
GripErgonomicsWet insulated glovesThe key can be pinched and pulled without slipping
TetherErgonomicsThread the coiled lanyard clipThe clip passes through the 4.5 mm hole and swivels freely
  • Too tightLower stem_width and stem_thickness by 0.1 to 0.2 mm; PETG prints slightly oversize.
  • Latch missesMove stem_cutout_start. The stem length follows on its own.
  • Stem snapsRaise stem_edge_rim or stem_thickness, and add perimeters before adding infill.
  • SlipperyRaise rib_depth and rib_width, or pick the deep grooves preset.

11GlossarySOURCE▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section. Each term's Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
ThingiversePrintingA website where people share 3D printable models. Izzy mentioned an existing key model there; it was not used for this entry.
Push keyPartA safety key that is pushed straight into a switch to let the machine run and pulled out to stop it. It does not turn.
StemPartThe thin blade of the key that goes into the switch barrel.
GuardPartThe collar between handle and stem. It stops the key at the right depth and is the datum for all stem distances.
HandlePartThe grip end of the key, enlarged here for insulated gloves.
Lanyard holePartThe hole through the handle for a coiled tether that keeps the key attached to the machine.
Grip groovesPartShallow channels cut across the grip faces so wet gloves do not slip. The spec calls this the grip texture.
Switch barrelPartThe spring-loaded socket on the snow thrower that the stem slides into.
Locking windowStem featuresThe square hole near the stem tip that the switch’s spring latch drops into to hold the key.
Edge rimStem featuresThe full-thickness wall that runs around the outside of the stem.
Recessed webStem featuresThe thinner floor inside the rim. Rim plus web give the stem an I-beam section: stiff, with less plastic.
Side notchStem featuresA shallow cut in each long edge of the stem, an arc followed by a ramp back to the edge.
Diamond tipStem featuresThe tapered last 5.5 mm of the stem. Read here as a wedge that thins toward the nose.
ChamferStem featuresA small flat cut across a sharp edge, here at 45 degrees, so the edge enters the barrel smoothly.
LatchStem featuresThe spring-loaded catch inside the switch that engages the locking window.
ParametricCADDriven by named values. Change a value and every feature that depends on it updates.
DatumCADThe reference surface that distances are measured from. Here it is the guard face on the stem side.
Bilateral symmetryCADThe left half is the mirror image of the right half about the long axis.
FusionCADAutodesk Fusion, the CAD program the spec is written around. F360 is its older short name.
STEPCADA neutral CAD exchange file that carries exact solids rather than a mesh. Not produced by this page.
TangentCADTwo curves meeting with no corner, each continuing the other’s direction.
STLMeshThe standard 3D printing file: a surface made only of triangles.
OBJMeshA mesh file that can keep four-sided faces and named groups, which makes it easier to edit than an STL.
QuadMeshA four-sided face. A mesh that is mostly quads is cleaner to read and to edit than one made of triangles.
WatertightMeshA mesh with no gaps: every edge is shared by exactly two faces. Slicers need this to tell inside from outside.
MeshMeshA surface described by flat faces joined at shared corner points.
PETGPrintingA tough, slightly flexible printing plastic that handles cold and impact better than PLA.
PerimetersPrintingThe outline passes a printer lays down around each layer before filling the inside. More perimeters make thin walls solid.
Gyroid infillPrintingA wavy, three-dimensional fill pattern inside a print that is strong in every direction.
SupportsPrintingThrowaway material printed under parts that would otherwise hang in the air.
SlicerPrintingThe program that turns a model into printer instructions. Orca and PrusaSlicer are two.
Injection moldedPrintingMade by forcing melted plastic into a steel mould, the way the original key was made.
OrthographicViewerA view with no perspective: parallel edges stay parallel, so proportions can be judged by eye.
Section cutViewerA view that slices the model on a plane to show what is inside.
